answer: Each epoch pulse opens an admission auction of 100 identities. Bids are sealed; winners lock 20-epoch bonds, then bids surface on a crystal ledger. An attacker buying 1,000 fakes bids against itself, so the price climbs a canyon wall: the k-th costs 50+(k-1) credits, locking 549,500 against a 40,000 pool. Rented bids fail: the bond is tied to the winner's key and burns if caught. Honest agents pay one 50-credit bid once and keep a full share.
